findings.title: The named entry governs the coming act
findings.claim: The invocation's raised divine designation and paired mercy names place the later praise, worship, petition, and guidance under one named addressee, changing the opening from a detachable preface into an oriented act of speech.
findings.mechanism: The focus forms for the divine name, the name-designation, and mercy are encountered before the supplied later acts; the name-to-act order lets those acts read as performed under the invoked designation while mercy remains their entering register.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel what 'in the name' does to the next acts: it aligns them before they unfold and keeps the addressee present.
findings.containment: This is a qualified global resonance inferred from the reader-walk record and supplied pericope order. The later acts remain contextual triggers; the name is not being made a complete substitute for them, and unlisted name or mercy senses are not activated.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus carriers and QAC returns are supplied, but the semantic arrow from the opening to later acts is an unbound reader-walk inference and the cited connection targets lack target morphology.
